newsitem.title: USA: Omnicare to buy American Medserve.
newsitem.headline: Omnicare to buy American Medserve.

text.p: Omnicare Inc. said Friday it has agreed to acquire American Medserve Corp., another provider of pharmacy services for long-term care facilities, for about $223 million in cash.
In addition, Omnicare will assume American Medserve's long-term debt of about $11.6 million.
The acquisition will mark Omnicare's entry into six new states and broaden the Cincinnati-based company's network of existing pharmacies in five other states.
Under the agreement, Omnicare will make a cash tender offer of $18 a share for all of the outstanding American Medserve shares. The offer will remain open for 20 business days, unless extended.
American Medserve stock rose $2 to $17.50 on Nasdaq in late trading. Omnicare slid 62.5 cents to $30 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The acquisition is expected to have no effect on Omnicare's earnings per share in 1997, and will boost results in 1998 due to economies of scale and cost synergies, it said.
The deal, which has been approved by directors of both companies, is subject to the tender of a majority of the outstanding American Medserve shares and regulatory approval.

American Medserve, based in Naperville, Ill., provides pharmacy and related services to about 51,400 residents in 720 long-term care facilities in 11 states. It has annualized revenues of about $144 million.

With the acquisition, Omnicare will provide pharmacy and related consulting services to some 413,000 residents in over 5,100 long-term care facilities in 35 states. It would have annual revenues of more than $950 million.
